what_happened: An the person running Athena corrected their own earlier log entry. The batch had been running one job, not two. Two writer builds at once take 12 to 13 GB each and nearly fill the disk, because each writer keeps its own build folder. So a max_concurrency of 2 is only safe for disk once writers use the shared build slots. No job was rejected or failed. This was a correction to a record.
cause: Athena does not show how many jobs a batch is running, and it does not model per-job disk use. Build output is not shared yet, so the disk cost of concurrency depends on the the person running Athena's memory of the setup. The the person running Athena therefore reasoned about the safe limit from assumption and had to correct the record afterwards. The parallelism limit stays an unmeasured, hand-set number tied to a disk limit that nothing enforces.
prevention: Add a code check at admission and at drain start that measures free disk and the observed or configured per-job build size. It would refuse or cap max_concurrency when free disk is below concurrency times that size. Also show the running job count and the effective concurrency in the drain status, so an entry about concurrency can be checked against real state. A shared build slot scheme would later lower the per-job size, and the check would then permit 2 on its own.
proposed_request: Make the queue drain keep its parallelism within what the disk can hold. Outcome: before it starts a job, the drain measures free disk and compares it with the build size a writer job needs, using the measured size of recent writer builds (about 12 to 13 GB each today). It starts another job only if both fit with a safety margin, and it runs fewer jobs at once otherwise, even when [parallel] max_concurrency is higher. The drain status shows how many jobs are running, the effective concurrency, free disk, and the reason when it ran fewer than configured. Acceptance: (1) a test with simulated free disk shows two jobs start when space allows and one when it does not; (2) the status output names the limiting reason; (3) the check holds on the default serial path (max_concurrency = 1) too, and changes nothing there; (4) no hand edit of athena.toml is needed to stay safe.
